A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LZ Penalty research. All 13 pages of v2 and 14 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original AIME/GPQA accuracy and repetition experiments, appendix penalty sweeps, and SGLang latency/throughput measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and measurements and adds a documented Cursor/Gemini repetition example.

M1.justification: The simulated LZSS compressor, sliding window and buffer, marginal-codelength calculation, and logit adjustment remain unchanged, including Equations 3–14.

E1.justification: AIME/GPQA benchmark coverage remains unchanged. Appendix A.1 in v3 adds a software-debugging interaction using Gemini-2.5-Pro in Cursor agent mode, extending the documented scenarios through an illustrative failure case without evaluating LZ there.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain the no-penalty baseline, repetition penalty, and frequency penalty. Gemini-2.5-Pro appears only in the added failure example, not as a comparator against LZ.

E3.justification: The benchmark protocols retain the 24k token limit, top-p 0.95, top-k 40, LZ strength 0.15, window 512, and buffer 32. Penalty sweeps and throughput benchmark settings also match; the added screenshot specifies no new controlled evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.1 and Figure 3 document repeated task-completion messages in a deployed coding agent, adding a concrete failure case outside the existing benchmarks. The existing temperature and penalty-strength analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark averages and empirical standard deviations over five runs, with the same accuracy error-bar practice. No additional seed information, uncertainty procedure, or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: The benchmark plot images are identical after matching their reordered placement, and Table 1 retains every numerical value. v3 adds qualitative evidence of Gemini-2.5-Pro producing repetitive completion messages in Cursor; it reports no new LZ performance result.

T1.justification: The definitions, propositions, and LZ derivation retain their mathematical substance. Proposition 3 drops the repeated 'prefix-free' qualifier, but Definition 5 still assumes complete prefix codes, so the formal assumption is preserved.

C1.justification: The central claim that LZ enables greedy reasoning without degenerate repetition or capability loss remains unchanged. The introduction broadens the stated problem by asserting that frontier models can repeat even at higher temperatures in deployed services.

C2.justification: v3 removes the limitations paragraph explaining that algorithmic determinism may be unnecessary with caching or fixed seeds and insufficient under hardware nondeterminism. The empirical mechanism explanations remain, but these substantive applicability qualifications are lost.

D1.justification: v3 removes v2's repository pointers for tginart/sglang and tginart/lz-penalty. Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain; the change concerns access information, without establishing that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds Cursor and Gemini-2.5-Pro source pointers supporting the deployment example. The 25 bibliography entries and substantive positioning against earlier sampling and compression research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes the introductory contribution summary and limitations paragraph, adds an appendix subsection, switches to author-year citations, and makes small spelling and author-name edits. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 changes typography, text widths, heading styles, header rules, and figure/table sizing and placement throughout the document. It adds screenshot Figure 3 and reverses the appendix heatmap order. Figure 4's revised caption incorrectly describes frequency-penalty rows as repetition-penalty rows.

improvement.justification: The new Cursor/Gemini example makes the motivation more concrete, but v3 removes useful determinism limitations and the repository access pointers, while introducing a misleading Figure 4 caption. With the method and quantitative validation unchanged, these losses in reproducibility and interpretive precision outweigh the limited benefit of the added example.
